# skill-curator

Audit, evaluate, merge, and refresh a library of agent skills. Use when asked to review or clean up installed skills, check whether two skills collide on the same trigger, vet or compare third-party skills before installing, merge duplicates, harvest material from skill repos into an existing skill, or check a skill's upstream sources for updates. NOT for authoring a new skill from scratch (use skill-creator) and NOT for writing the subject-matter content inside one.

## What is in here

`SKILL.md` is the skill itself and the file the model reads first.

Reference files, read on demand rather than loaded up front:

- [`references/harvest-log.md`](references/harvest-log.md) — Harvest Log Format
- [`references/maintenance.md`](references/maintenance.md) — Maintenance
- [`references/security-screen.md`](references/security-screen.md) — Security Screen for Third-Party Skills

Bundled scripts, which the skill calls rather than reimplementing:

- [`scripts/audit.py`](scripts/audit.py) — Mechanical half of a skill-library audit. Findings, never scores.
- [`scripts/overlap.py`](scripts/overlap.py) — Find verbatim phrasing shared between a skill and its sources.

## Evidence

[`evals/`](evals/) holds 7 evals with their expectations and wrong-answer controls. Each control is a plausible wrong answer that the graders must fail, so an eval that cannot fail is caught rather than counted.

Scores, method and the correction history are in the repository's `EVALS.md`. Read that before quoting a number: it records which rounds are unsafe to cite and why.

## Where it came from

[`ATTRIBUTION.md`](ATTRIBUTION.md) records what this skill descends from, what was taken from whom, and what was measured rather than borrowed.

## Install

```bash
npx skills install skill-curator
```

Or copy this directory into your agent's skills directory. The skill is Markdown plus readable Python; nothing here runs at install time.
